llm.summary: This PDF skill performs useful document operations, but it is misleadingly framed as local/no-upload while its scripts send full documents to a configured HTTP Stirling-PDF service by default.

dimensions.detail: The PDF operations are purpose-aligned, but the artifacts repeatedly claim local processing and no uploads while the scripts use curl to POST input files to a Stirling-PDF API endpoint, with a default private-network HTTP URL.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill documents many PDF mutation and security operations, including decrypt, encrypt, watermarking, conversion, OCR, merge, and compression, but does not give clear runtime warnings that files are uploaded or that outputs may materially change document content, format, or security properties.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package is a simple skill with shell helper scripts and no dependency installation or persistence hooks; it requires users to supply STIRLING_API_KEY and optionally a base URL.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Using a Stirling-PDF API is coherent for this toolkit, but the default http://192.168.31.158:3998 endpoint and plaintext HTTP are under-scoped for sensitive PDFs and may target an unintended internal host if installed elsewhere.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background persistence, privilege escalation, or credential storage was found, but the scripts read an API key from the environment and pass it to the remote service on each request.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use this skill with a Stirling-PDF server you control, set the base URL explicitly, prefer HTTPS or localhost, and avoid sensitive legal, financial, medical, or business PDFs unless you are comfortable sending the full files and API key to that service. Work on copies and verify outputs before replacing originals.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The concern is supported: despite local/no-upload claims, both helper scripts upload user-supplied PDF files to a network API endpoint.
[SDI-2] expected: An API key is expected for a Stirling-PDF API integration and is disclosed in the environment section, but it compounds the concern because the remote service boundary is not clearly explained.
[SQP-2] expected: PDF modification features are expected for this toolkit, but the lack of clear warnings around upload, irreversible document changes, and security-altering operations is a real under-disclosure issue.
